---
title: "Roadmap"
subtitle: "What is next for DeskPets, roughly in order"
---

DeskPets works today, and this is where I want to take it. There are no dates, because it is a personal project, and the order can change.

## Next: an installer

A one-click Windows installer, so you don't need Python or pixi to try it. This is the current focus. See [Download](download.qmd).

## Then: making it solid

- **Check the things a short test can't show:** long-running sessions, sleep and resume, and multiple monitors.
- **Tune the thresholds on real workloads.** The defaults are tuned to one machine, and the swap limit is still a guess.
- **Support more hardware.** A reliable CPU temperature on Windows, and GPUs that aren't NVIDIA.
- **Fix the known art issues:** restore the jump's lift, and redraw the stroll so it can loop.
- **Give the sad animation a real trigger.** Today it only plays from the tray menu.
- **Sharper pixels** on displays scaled to 150%.

Most of these are the entries on [Known limitations](/project/known-limitations.qmd).

## Later 

- **A chat window** where Layla and Chico connect to language models, with carefully scoped tools. It is a direction and not a feature yet. See [Agentic AI](about.qmd#agentic-ai) on the About page.
- **Linux and macOS,** as time allows as some of my friends with cats use these. Their window handling needs dedicated platform work and is not a simple packaging change. But if interest is high, I can prioritize it.

## Suggest something

If you'd like to see something here, or something on this list moved up, [open an issue](https://github.com/Suyash-Naik/DeskPets/issues).
